Package net.sourceforge.plantuml.style.parser2

Class StyleQuery

java.lang.Object
net.sourceforge.plantuml.style.parser2.StyleQuery
public final class StyleQuery extends Object
What a StyleAtomTrie is asked to resolve: the element's tags (its SName set plus any stereotypes, e.g. what the legacy StyleSignatureBasic calls snames/stereotypes) and its LevelConstraint (its mindmap/wbs depth and whether this is an ancestor-inheritance lookup -- see LevelConstraint).

    • withStereotype

      public StyleQuery withStereotype(String stereotype)
      This same query, additionally requiring stereotype -- e.g. so a "frequent use" factory that starts from a plain, stereotype-less query (the common case, since most such factories are called with no stereotype in hand yet) can still fold one in once the caller has it, the way StyleSignature.addStereotype does for the legacy signature. stereotype is cleaned exactly as StyleAtom.ofStereotype(java.lang.String) cleans it (see there for why), so passing it in raw, un-lower-cased text is fine. Requiring several stereotypes at once (an element tagged with more than one, e.g. <<foo>><<bar>>) is just calling this again on the result, since a TreeSet silently dedupes a stereotype already present.

    • forStereotypeItself

      public StyleQuery forStereotypeItself(Stereotype stereo)
      This same query, additionally requiring every one of stereo's labels at once, the same way withTOBECHANGED(Stereotype) does -- but also requiring the special SName.stereotype tag, mirroring StyleSignature.forStereotypeItself: used to resolve the CSS-class-like rule for the stereotype itself (e.g. <<foo>>'s own .foo { ... } declaration), as opposed to a plain element carrying that stereotype.
